content.text:
## Recommended global conversion shortlist

For an existing **upper-upscale, full-service hotel**, owners should generally test both:

1. **Collection/soft brands**, which preserve the property’s identity and usually offer greater design flexibility; and  
2. **Traditional brands**, which provide clearer consumer positioning but may require more extensive brand-standard work.

### 1. Collection and soft brands—usually the best starting point

| Brand | Platform | Best suited to | Key consideration |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Autograph Collection** | Marriott | Distinctive urban hotels, historic assets and destination resorts | Strong option when the hotel has a compelling story, architecture and upscale F&B. Marriott positions its collection brands as an operating model for independent hotels. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Tribute Portfolio** | Marriott | Independent lifestyle and boutique upper-upscale hotels | Generally appropriate for a more approachable, lifestyle-oriented asset than Autograph; conversion-specific PIP and brand assessment processes apply. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/resourcefiles/fdd-document/2022-tribute-fdd.pdf?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Curio Collection by Hilton** | Hilton | Upper-upscale urban, resort and heritage properties | One of the strongest direct comparisons to Autograph; Hilton expressly identifies Curio as conversion-friendly and allows properties to retain their individual stories. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai)) |
| **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** | Hyatt | High-quality upper-upscale or luxury landmarks and resorts | Best for highly differentiated, story-rich properties capable of commanding a premium. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/theunboundcollectionbyhyatt?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Destination by Hyatt** | Hyatt | Resorts, retreats, residential resorts and destination-led hotels | Particularly relevant where recreation, wellness, golf, ski or resort programming is central to demand. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands/destinationbyhyatt?utm_source=openai)) |
| **JdV by Hyatt** | Hyatt | Smaller lifestyle and neighborhood hotels | Hyatt classifies JdV as upper-upscale, typically suited to approximately 50–250 rooms and a strong local personality. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **MGallery Collection** | Accor | Boutique upper-upscale hotels with design and historical character | Accor identifies MGallery as its upper-upscale collection brand and prioritizes conversions within its collection portfolio. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/collection-brands-handwritten-emblems-mgallery?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Vignette Collection** | IHG | Upper-upscale assets capable of moving toward luxury/lifestyle positioning | A flexible independent conversion brand that retains the hotel’s name, design and service identity; particularly attractive when a higher ADR repositioning is feasible. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/vignette-collection?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Radisson Collection** | Radisson Hotel Group | Iconic upper-upscale-to-luxury urban and resort assets | Allows individual identity, limited conversion costs and flexible contracts, with strongest platform relevance in EMEA and APAC. ([radissonhotels.com](https://www.radissonhotels.com/en-us/corporate/development-opportunities/our-brands?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Colbert Collection** | Minor Hotels | Independent lifestyle and luxury properties, particularly in Europe and the Middle East | A new conversion-led platform with simplified onboarding and flexible standards; consequently, it has less operating history than the established collections. ([minorhotels.com](https://www.minorhotels.com/en/development/colbert-collection?utm_source=openai)) |
| **Registry Collection Hotels** | Wyndham | Independent upper-upscale resorts and distinctive urban hotels | Wyndham explicitly positions Registry as an upper-upscale soft brand, although its system depth at this segment is smaller than Marriott’s or Hilton’s. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/brand/registry-collection-hotels/?utm_source=openai)) |

### 2. Conversion-oriented traditional brands

These should be considered when the asset has a relatively conventional room product, substantial meeting space, broad business demand, or insufficient individuality for a collection brand.

- **voco hotels — IHG:** One of the clearest conversion propositions in the market. It combines a hard-brand identity with relatively flexible design and operating standards. IHG describes voco as an upscale conversion brand with lower capital outlay than more prescriptive alternatives. ([development.ihg.com](https://development.ihg.com/hotel-brands/voco-hotels?utm_source=openai))
- **DoubleTree by Hilton:** A well-established conversion brand for conventional full-service hotels, especially in commercial, airport and secondary urban markets. Hilton continues to record conversions under DoubleTree globally. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/hilton-culture/qa-gary-steffen-on-pride-leadership-and-brand-updates?utm_source=openai))
- **Delta Hotels by Marriott:** Appropriate for straightforward, business-oriented full-service hotels where operational simplicity is more important than lifestyle differentiation. Marriott’s franchise materials explicitly accommodate conversions. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/resourcefiles/fdd-document/2023-delta-fdd-3-31-2023.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Crowne Plaza:** Relevant for large corporate, meetings and airport hotels, although the owner should carefully model the renovation scope associated with the brand’s evolving product standards. IHG continues to position Crowne Plaza within its global premium portfolio. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2025/ihg-hotels-and-resorts-conversion-friendly-brands-fuel-growth-opportunities-for-owners?utm_source=openai))
- **Hyatt Regency:** Best for larger urban, convention and resort assets with meaningful meetings, F&B and group demand; Hyatt indicates a broad typical range of 200–2,000 rooms. ([hyatt.com](https://www.hyatt.com/development/ourbrands?utm_source=openai))
- **Pullman or Mövenpick — Accor:** Strong alternatives in markets where Accor has significant distribution, especially Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific. Accor identifies both as premium brands and specifically recognizes Mövenpick as conversion-friendly. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/500-premium-hotels-milestone-camil-yazbeck-benoit-racle?utm_source=openai))
- **Radisson Blu:** Particularly compelling in Europe, the Middle East, Africa and parts of Asia; Radisson identifies it as an upper-upscale brand with an easy-to-adopt design scheme. ([radissonhotels.com](https://www.radissonhotels.com/en-us/corporate/development-opportunities/our-brands?utm_source=openai))
- **NH Collection:** A credible upper-upscale conversion option, especially in Europe, Latin America and selected Asian markets. Minor has specifically identified NH Collection for upper-upscale conversion opportunities. ([minorhotels.com](https://www.minorhotels.com/en/development?utm_source=openai))

## Shortlist by asset profile

### Distinctive urban or heritage hotel
Prioritize:

1. Autograph Collection  
2. Curio Collection  
3. The Unbound Collection  
4. MGallery  
5. Vignette Collection  
6. Radisson Collection  

### Lifestyle or neighborhood boutique hotel
Prioritize:

1. Tribute Portfolio  
2. JdV by Hyatt  
3. Curio Collection  
4. MGallery  
5. Hotel Indigo  
6. Tapestry Collection—if an upscale rather than upper-upscale position is acceptable  

### Conventional corporate or meetings hotel
Prioritize:

1. DoubleTree  
2. Delta Hotels  
3. voco  
4. Crowne Plaza  
5. Hyatt Regency  
6. Pullman, Mövenpick or Radisson Blu, depending on geography  

### Destination resort
Prioritize:

1. Destination by Hyatt  
2. Autograph Collection  
3. Curio Collection  
4. The Unbound Collection  
5. MGallery  
6. Vignette Collection  
7. Registry Collection  

## How an owner should make the final selection

Brand evaluation should be based on **incremental asset value**, not simply the largest loyalty program. Require each shortlisted company to provide a ten-year underwriting case covering:

- Brand-generated room-night contribution by source market
- Expected ADR and occupancy uplift
- Base, incentive, franchise, marketing, loyalty and reservation fees
- Property-improvement-plan cost per key
- Required room closures and renovation downtime
- F&B, meeting-space, club-lounge and staffing requirements
- Franchise versus management availability
- Contract term, area protection and performance termination rights
- Owner approval rights over design and senior management
- Forecast EBITDA after all system costs
- Exit capitalization-rate and buyer-pool implications

**Practical recommendation:** begin the process with **Autograph, Curio, Unbound, MGallery, Vignette and voco**, then add the strongest regionally relevant alternatives. Run these against at least two traditional flags such as **DoubleTree, Delta, Crowne Plaza, Hyatt Regency, Pullman or Radisson Blu**. This creates a meaningful comparison between identity-preserving flexibility and the potentially stronger recognition of a conventional global brand.
